note: Sogdian merchants formed extensive trading colonies in Chang'an and along the Silk Road; their language served as a lingua franca of Tang Central Asian administration. The two polities maintained a symbiotic commercial relationship until the An Lushan Rebellion and subsequent Arab conquest of Sogdiana severed direct contact.

_quarry.structural_significance: Sogdian intermediation enabled Tang projection into Central Asia and the transmission of Manichaeism, Nestorian Christianity, and Buddhist iconography into China.
